chunks: What Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿImrān ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿImrān al-Ashʿarī, from some of our companions, raising it to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

The camel-driver and the muleteer, when the travel presses on earnestly with them, should perform qasr between the two stopping places, and they should perform the prayer in full at the stopping place.

key_terms.السَّيْرُ: travel or movement on the road
key_terms.الْجَمَّالُ: the camel-driver; a person whose occupation involves transport by camel
key_terms.الْمَنْزِلَيْنِ: the two stopping places or stages of travel
key_terms.الْمَنْزِلِ: the stopping place, lodging, or station
key_terms.الْمُكَارِي: the muleteer or hired transport driver
key_terms.جَدَّ: became earnest or pressing; here, when the journey became active and continuous
key_terms.فَلْيَقْصُرَا: let them shorten; i.e., perform qasr prayer
key_terms.يُتِمَّا: let them complete; i.e., perform the prayer in full

ai.seo_question: When should a camel-driver or muleteer shorten or complete the prayer during travel?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the salat of professional travelers such as the camel-driver and the muleteer. It states that they shorten the prayer while traveling between stopping places, but perform it in full once they are at the stopping place.
